memory_update.text: SPSC should be the primary underfollowed direct candidate for retailer-supplier connectivity networks; it has public evidence of 50,000+ recurring-revenue customers and deep retail-network positioning.

OTEX is a relevant but less pure mid-cap infrastructure candidate because OpenText Business Network / Trading Grid has very large EDI trading-partner scale, but exposure is diluted inside a diversified software portfolio.

DSGX is a second-order network infrastructure candidate through logistics, ecommerce, B2B connectivity, and EDI messaging; verify how much of revenue is directly tied to retail-supplier EDI versus broader logistics/customs modules.

The scarce asset in this node is less physical capacity and more accumulated operational logic: retailer-specific maps, EDI documents, compliance rules, supplier onboarding data, and integrations across ERP, WMS, OMS, retail, grocery, CPG, and logistics systems.

Need further work on private competitors and potential public look-through exposures: TrueCommerce, Cleo, Rithum, Syndigo, Orderful, CommerceHub, InterTrade, and ERP/channel partners may affect public-company share and pricing power.

node: Retailer-supplier connectivity networks, EDI/API rails, compliance maps, and trading-partner data
summary: Expanded the stock universe around retailer-supplier connectivity and EDI/API compliance networks. The strongest direct underfollowed candidate is SPS Commerce, which appears closest to the node: retail-specific trading-partner connectivity, recurring revenue, and retailer/supplier compliance mappings. OpenText and Descartes are larger but relevant network infrastructure comparables through B2B integration, EDI, and global trading-partner networks. Manhattan Associates is included as a reference-adjacent second-order name because its order, store, warehouse, and omnichannel execution software touches the same operational layer, but it is less pure to the retailer-supplier EDI network chokepoint.
